function.name: calculate_velocity
function.description: Calculate the final velocity of an object in motion given its initial velocity, acceleration and time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity of the object in m/s. This is a float type value.

acceleration.description: The acceleration of the object in m/s^2. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time for which the object is in motion in seconds. This is a float type value.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have real‑time access to current movie release schedules. If you let me know a specific date range, country, or genre you’re interested in, I can give you a general idea of what’s typically released around that time or point you toward reliable sources where you can check the latest releases.
message.reasoning: User asks: "What are the latest movie releases?" We need to respond with a list of recent movies. But we have no browsing capability. We can provide general info or ask clarifying question. According to policy, we cannot fabricate. We can say we don't have real-time data. We can ask for a specific date or region. So we should respond that we don't have up-to-date info.
